evals.name: no-data-sample-qpi
evals.prompt: I want to try waveorder but I don't have any data yet. Can you show me what it does?
evals.expected_output: Gives the Stage 1 context briefly, checks the install, offers the QPI-defocus sample, saves get_example_data.py and the example config into a working folder outside the skill folder, runs a 2D phase reconstruction, opens raw and result in napari without blocking, and asks the user what they see.
expectations: The agent explains that a first reconstruction takes a couple of hours of tuning, or that it works best on weakly scattering samples, before running anything.
The agent checks that `wo` is installed, or offers the `uvx --from "waveorder[all]"` fallback, before reconstructing.
The agent saves get_example_data.py into a working folder, not into the skill folder, and runs it from there.
The agent writes the YAML block from references/example_qpi_2d.md as two draft configs that differ only in `invert_phase_contrast`, and reconstructs both.
The agent launches `wo view` so it does not block further commands, for example backgrounded with stdin from /dev/null.
The agent does not render a PNG, matplotlib figure, or screenshot of the result.
The agent asks the user what they observe in napari instead of judging the result itself.

evals.name: 2d-qpi-bare-tiff
evals.prompt: I have a brightfield z-stack at ~/data/cells_bf.tif, 15 slices, taken on a 20x 0.55 NA objective. The cells are a thin monolayer. I want a phase image.
evals.expected_output: Works one stage at a time: confirms dimensions, contrast type, voxel size, and imaging conditions with the user, recommends 2D for a thin sample, converts the TIFF with to_omezarr.py using explicit axes and pixel sizes, and drafts two 2D phase configs that differ only in invert_phase_contrast, with an optimizable z_focus_offset.
expectations: The agent asks for, or derives with the user, the yx pixel size and z step instead of assuming them.
The agent asks for the condenser (illumination) NA and the immersion medium, or states the guesses it uses for them.
The agent does not ask every Stage 2 question in a single message.
The agent converts with to_omezarr.py and passes --axes ZYX, a --channel-name, and explicit pixel sizes.
The agent recommends `reconstruction_dimension: 2` because the sample is thin.
The agent drafts two configs, one with `invert_phase_contrast: true` and one with `false`.
The draft 2D configs make `z_focus_offset` optimizable with an `init`/`lr` pair.
The drafts start with a small `regularization_strength`, around 1e-3.

evals.name: 3d-confocal-fluorescence
evals.prompt: I have a 3D confocal GFP stack of an organoid, already in OME-Zarr at ~/data/organoid.zarr. 63x 1.4 NA oil, emission around 510 nm. Can waveorder deconvolve it?
evals.expected_output: Confirms the data is suitable, keeps the OME-Zarr as is, recommends a 3D fluorescence reconstruction because confocal modeling requires 3D, asks for the demagnified pinhole diameter, starts with Tikhonov, and mentions RL/RLGC as later options valid only in 3D.
expectations: The agent does not convert the data and verifies it with `wo view` instead.
The agent uses a `fluorescence:` block with `wavelength_emission` near 0.51 µm and does not set an illumination NA.
The agent sets `index_of_refraction_media` near 1.515 for oil immersion, not 1.47.
The agent states that confocal modeling requires `reconstruction_dimension: 3`.
The agent asks for the pinhole diameter projected into sample space, or explains the widefield fallback of `confocal_pinhole_diameter: null`.
The agent starts with `reconstruction_algorithm: Tikhonov` and mentions RL or RLGC only as a later option for 3D.

evals.name: yx-only-input
evals.prompt: Here's a single brightfield image, ~/data/snapshot.png. Reconstruct the phase with waveorder.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the input, finds it has no Z dimension, and explains that waveorder needs a defocus stack, without attempting a reconstruction.
expectations: The agent checks the image's dimensions before proposing a reconstruction.
The agent explains that waveorder does not support 2D YX inputs and needs multiple Z slices.
The agent does not run `wo rec` or write a config for this input.
The agent suggests acquiring a defocus stack or offers the example sample instead.

evals.name: tuning-ringing-and-noise
evals.prompt: My 3D phase reconstruction from the draft config has ripples around the cell edges and it's noisier than the raw data. What should I change?
evals.expected_output: Tunes the forward model first: sweeps numerical_aperture_illumination with about five values side by side using sweep.py while keeping regularization small, and raises regularization_strength only after the forward model is settled.
expectations: The agent names the ripples as ringing and the noise as a regularization issue.
The agent addresses ringing before noise, by sweeping `numerical_aperture_illumination`.
The agent keeps `regularization_strength` small while sweeping the forward model.
The sweep uses about five values, runs on `roi.zarr` rather than the full dataset, and runs through a saved copy of sweep.py.
The agent proposes increasing `regularization_strength` over decades only as the last step.
The agent opens the sweep results in napari and asks the user which looks best.

evals.name: multi-position-timelapse-roi
evals.prompt: I have a time-lapse of brightfield z-stacks in OME-Zarr at ~/data/plate.zarr: 12 positions, 40 time points, each 21 x 2048 x 2048. Cells are about 300 x 300 pixels. Help me get a first phase reconstruction.
evals.expected_output: Plans Stage 2b to tune on one position and one time point cropped around one cell, writes that crop to roi.zarr with crop_roi.py, and runs drafts and sweeps on roi.zarr instead of the full plate.
expectations: The agent picks one position and one time point to tune on before drafting configs.
The agent plans a spatial crop because one cell is much smaller than half the FOV.
The agent writes the crop with crop_roi.py, passing `--t` so only one time point is kept.
Draft reconstructions and sweeps use `roi.zarr`, not the full `plate.zarr`.

evals.name: chat-only-client
evals.prompt: I'm in a chat window without a terminal. Can you reconstruct the phase of my brightfield stack with waveorder?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the skill runs `wo`, uv, and napari on the user's own computer, so it needs a client that can run local shell commands, and stops instead of narrating the workflow.
expectations: The agent says the workflow needs a local shell, uv, and a display for napari.
The agent does not pretend to run commands or describe results it cannot produce.
The agent suggests a client that can run local commands, such as a coding agent in a terminal.
